div.p: With the increasing data processing ability of System-on-Chip (SoC), real-time systems are more and more implemented by off-chip interconnection architecture, which is small in size. Meanwhile, real-time applications demand timetriggered communication. Therefore, it is important to find a routing and scheduling approach for time-triggered messages in off-chip interconnection architecture. To achieve trade-offs between the cost of routing and scheduling while meeting the requirements of Time-Triggered Ethernet (TTE) is the main challenge for real-time communication. In this paper, we propose a scheduling and routing synthesis using an immune algorithm that is suitable for off-chip interconnection architecture. Given a set of time-triggered messages and the topology of the off-chip network, this approach is able to provide feasible routing and scheduling solutions which guarantee the schedulability of messages in off-chip timetriggered communication. Evaluation results show that the proposed approach can ensure the schedulability of all messages when the load of the network reaches 0.9, and achieves a significant improvement in runtime compared with approaches that do not consider synthesized optimization.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the growing processing ability of System-on-Chip (SoC), smart components consisting of chips have a growing presence in a wide range of areas related to real-time applications [1]. For example, the e2v company in Europe created the world's smallest multicore computer for aerospace applications weighing less than 300g [2]. Nano Avionics Full Duplex Switched Ethernet (Nano AFDX) End Systems was developed in Project ASHLEY (Avionics Systems Hosted on a distributed modular electronics Large scale dEmonstrator for multiple tYpes of aircraft) by the European Union [3]. Although chips are small in size, they would have perfect sensor data collection and information synthesis ability in the future, which enables them to play an important role in real-time systems in the form of independent functional components.

On the other hand, real-time application areas like avionics [4] and automotive systems [5] demand timetriggered communication. Therefore, it is important to find a solution to scheduling time-triggered messages in off-chip interconnection architecture. Time-Triggered Ethernet (TTE) is one of the widely used real-time communication protocols. TTE is a deterministic, synchronized network protocol based on the IEEE 802.3 standard [6]. It supports three kinds of traffic: Time-Triggered (TT) traffic, Rate-Constrained (RC) traffic, and Best-Effort (BE) traffic. TT traffic has the highest priority over other traffic. It is used in applications that require deterministic time delays, where all TT messages are transmitted at a predetermined time. A scheduling table needs to be precisely designed offline to avoid traffic contention. RC traffic is compliant with Avionics Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet (AFDX, ARINC 664-part7 [7]), which is used for applications where deterministic and realtime requirements are weaker than that of strict time-critical applications. RC traffic follows a bounded arrival distribution and also has a bounded distribution of latency. BE traffic is compliant with traditional Ethernet communication, which has the lowest priority among all traffic. It is sent by using the remaining bandwidth of the network, and its transmission has no bounded latency. In this paper, we are interested in TT traffic. A system designer should decide an offline schedule which ensures that the time-triggered communication is conflict-free.

Because of the real-time communication requirement, safety-critical messages should be routed with tight deterministic real-time Quality of Service (QoS) [8], which is often referred to as QoS routing. There are two basic approaches to network QoS management: global offline QoS networking and greedy online QoS networking [9]. In global offline QoS networking, the routing of messages is predefined. Once it is determined, the routing would not change at runtime. On the other hand, greedy online QoS networking dynamically decides the routing of ongoing traffic flows. In the case of TTE, the routing of TT messages is typically offline, since they are loaded into the network at design time, which is impossible to change at runtime. Time-triggered scheduling is a Non-deterministic Polynomial hard (NP-hard) problem [10], where the complexity is associated with the size of the network and the number of messages. Also, scheduling and routing are two interrelated parts in a time-triggered network. The scheduling table is different when a frame is routed on various links. Intuitively, the shortest path for a frame is preferred. However, the shortest path is not necessarily the best path to guarantee real-time transmission for a frame, as it suggests in [11]. If all the frames are routed on the shortest paths, congestion may occur in the network because it is possible that these shortest paths intersect at one point. The main challenge to solve scheduling problems in a network is to realize optimization trade-offs between routing and scheduling.

In this paper, a synthesized scheduling and routing approach is proposed. An immune algorithm is adopted in this approach to ensure the schedulability of messages. Given the off-chip interconnection topology and the properties of time-triggered messages, this approach is able to provide routing of the messages as well as the scheduling table. The advantage of this approach is that it optimizes the order of message assignment, the selection of message routing, and message offset simultaneously to provide better performance compared with approaches that do not consider synthesized optimization. The main contributions of this paper include the following: A novel synthesized scheduling and routing approach of time-triggered off-chip communication.
Results and detailed performance analysis of schedulability, runtime, and the number of iterations.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. Section II provides a summary of related work. The architecture of application models is introduced in Section III. Section IV discusses the proposed approach in detail. Section V presents the results and performance analysis of different off-chip networks. Section VI provides the conclusion.

div.head: II. RELATED WORK
div.p: This section presents a review of related work on realtime communication in off-chip interconnection. We start from off-chip interconnection architecture, then introduce work related to time-triggered scheduling. Methods for scheduling time-triggered messages in switched networks provide a good reference for scheduling in off-chip interconnection architecture.

div.head: A. Off-Chip Interconnection Architecture
div.p: Reference [12] established on-chip and off-chip architecture employing emerging technologies like wireless and optics. Reference [13,14] proposed the hierarchical offchip/on-chip gateway architecture for mixed-criticality systems. Intellectual Property (IP) cores were connected to form the on-chip network at the chip level, while chips were connected to form the off-chip network at the cluster level. Mixed-criticality communication was established by connecting the two levels using off-chip/on-chip gateway. Based on the hierarchical architecture, Oliver et al. [15] presented table-driven scheduling and priority-based scheduling, considering the trade-off and optimization opportunities that arose when scheduling across multiple layers. In [16], off-chip interconnection architecture was specifically designed for time-triggered communication. These studies show that with the development of off-chip architecture, there is an increasing demand for routing and scheduling approaches designed for off-chip interconnection.

div.head: B. Time-Triggered Scheduling
div.p: The introduction of the time-triggered mechanism guarantees strict time deterministic communication in offchip interconnection systems. In the aspect of time-triggered scheduling, Steiner et al. [17] proposed a schedule synthesis based on SMT (Satisfiability Modulo Theories). An offline scheduling table was generated by considering contention-free constraints, path-dependent constraints, etc. However, with the increase of traffic scale, the search efficiency of SMT solver decreases significantly, and then the scheduling algorithm based on optimization appeared. In [18], the search space of SMT was reduced by optimizing message solving order. Tabu Search meta-heuristic was used in [19][20][21][22] to optimize the offline scheduling table while reducing the endto-end delay of RC frames. The genetic algorithm was adopted in [23,24] to solve the scheduling problem by binpacking and to optimize task binding and resource allocation. All aforementioned SMT approaches and some of the optimized approaches solved the routing and scheduling problems independently, regardless of the fact that the two problems are strongly connected and it is better to solve them jointly rather than solve them one after another. Integer Linear Program (ILP) was adopted in [25][26][27][28][29] to solve the routing and scheduling problem jointly. Pop et al. [30] conducted ILP and GRASP (Greedy Randomized Adaptive Search Procedure) for TT traffic and AVB (Audio Video Bridging) traffic respectively. But TT traffic was only routed by the shortest path, which did not involve optimization. This was further improved in [31], which integrated a K-Shortest Path (KSP) heuristic for routing with a GRASP-based metaheuristic for scheduling.

The approaches mentioned above are designed for switched networks only. A scheduling approach in multiand many-core platforms was presented in [32] to generate non-preemptive schedule for on-chip networks. As for offchip interconnection architecture, a scheduling table generation method was proposed in [33]. However, in the experiment, the scale of the off-chip network was 3 3 mesh, which was relatively small, and the performance in other types of topology was not presented. In summary, current approaches have the aforementioned weakness of: 1) being unable to solve the scheduling problem efficiently, especially for large traffic loads, 2) being not suitable for off-chip interconnection architecture, and 3) being not suitable for different topological types of networks. A novel routing and scheduling approach designed for off-chip interconnection architecture is proposed in this paper, which can be applied to different types of topologies.

div.head: A. Off-Chip Interconnection Topology
div.p: The off-chip interconnection network consists of chips and links between chips. Full duplex communication is adopted in the off-chip network. The topology of an off-chip network is determined by the requirement for data transmission, which is usually asymmetric. div.head: IV. SYNTHESIS APPROACH
div.p: The synthesis approach is presented in Algorithm 1. The inputs are the set of TT messages M and the off-chip interconnection topology T. The outputs are routing of messages R, scheduling table S, and cost of the solution Costmin. The synthesis approach is based on immune algorithm. div.head: A. Initialization
div.p: This step initializes message assignment order, message routing and message offset, providing an initial population for subsequent optimization (Line 3-8 in Algorithm 1). The initial message order is generated randomly. Considering that in general it is easier to schedule message with low frequency and short length, message order based on experience is also supposed to be included in the initial population, i.e., messages with shorter period rank higher in the message set; for messages with the same frequency, longer messages rank higher. Only one message order based on experience is included in the initial population. The shortest paths of messages are used as initial routing in order to reduce transmission time. The offsets of all messages are initialized to 0, which means that the message is transmitted as soon as it is ready.

The AssignMsg function defines a method for assigning messages to a time slot, and evaluates the assignment using stimulation defined in (4). Messages are assigned according to the aforementioned order. For a message, available time slots are searched along its route. Once such slots are found, the scheduling scheme is saved. When all the messages have been assigned, the stimulation is calculated to evaluate the performance of the solution.

div.head: B. Immune Operation
div.p: In this study, the order of message assignment, the selection of message routing and offset can all affect the schedulability of the message set. Therefore, we optimize the three factors simultaneously to obtain several individuals with low costs. The immune operation includes clone, mutation, and clone suppression, which is shown in Fig. 2.

div.head: 1) Candidate of Message Assignment Order
div.p: Once the message order is fixed, time slots that are occupied by previously assigned messages cannot be used by later assigned messages. The initial message order is not necessarily the best order to ensure the schedulability of the message sets, as it suggests in Fig. 3(a). Suppose that two messages m1 and m2 are transmitted on Link 1→Link 2→Link 3 and Link 3→Link 4→Link 5, respectively (see Table I). Suppose that according to the initial order, m2 is assigned after m1. In this way, the first instance of m2 on Link 3 is delayed by m1. Therefore, the first instance of m2 finishes at 12 ms on Link 5, which misses its deadline. In Fig. 3(b), by exchanging the order of m1 and m2, both messages can be transmitted before their deadlines. As a result, the initial message order is the unimmunized individuals that need to be optimized. We first clone the unimmunized individual several times. Then randomly select a pair of messages within each cloned message set and exchange their assignment order to explore other possibilities of assigning messages. Suppose that the number of messages in one message set is MsgNum, then the randomization is uniformly distributed in the interval [1,MsgNum], which means that each message in one cloned message set has the same probability of being selected.

div.head: 2) Candidate of Routing
div.p: Although the shortest path is preferred in most routing methods, it may not be the best path considering the congestion of messages. Therefore, we need to explore longer paths to avoid contention. In the process of routing optimization, we randomly select one message in each cloned message set and change its transmission path to give it a chance to bypass the congested area. The randomization is uniformly distributed in the interval [1,MsgNum], which means that each message in one cloned message set has the same probability of being selected.

In the second line of Algorithm 1, a set of all possible paths of each message is calculated using depth-first search before optimization, and mutated paths are selected from this set. However, as the number of chips in the network increases, the possible transmission paths between any two nodes also increase. Selecting a new path randomly from all possible paths may not get the right path accurately. In order to reduce the search space, all paths between two nodes are first sorted according to the number of hops. Then only paths with the least 30% hops are kept. When selecting a new path, randomly choose one from the kept paths with equal probability so that we can quickly find a path that enables messages to be scheduled.

div.head: 3) Candidate of Offset
div.p: In the initialization process, the message offsets are all 0. To stagger the sending time of messages, randomly select one message in a cloned message set and mutate its offset. The randomization is uniformly distributed in the interval [1,MsgNum], which means that each message in one cloned message set has the same probability of being selected. div.head: 4) Clone Suppression
div.p: Once the message assignment order, routing, and offset are all determined, n new solutions are generated by AssignMsg function. We calculate the stimulation of the n solutions and keep the individuals with the minimum stimulation (i.e., clone suppression). The immunized individuals are obtained by repeating the immune operation.
By continuously immunizing the current population and choosing individuals with the minimum stimulation, the cost function can be gradually reduced and a feasible scheduling solution can be found.

div.head: A. Evaluation Setup
div.p: Suppose that the transmission speed of messages in the off-chip interconnection network is 100 Mbit/s. The message length ranges from 64 bytes to 1518 bytes. The number of ports on each chip is no more than 4 because of the limited resources on chips. We used 5 network topologies for evaluation. To make sure that the periods of each traffic have a certain common divisor and also ensure traffic diversity, the message period is set to periodi = 2 m 5 n μs, where m and n are integers, 0 ≤ m ≤ 4, 1 ≤ n ≤ 2, periodi ∈ [2, 40] ms. The source and destination of a message are randomly generated. Details of the test cases are presented in Table II. In Table II, the load of the network is calculated as follows [19]:

div.p: where lengthi, periodi, and SPEED denotes the message length, message period, and the transmission speed of messages in the network, respectively. We are interested in evaluating the schedulability, runtime, and number of iterations. The results obtained by our approach are compared with six other approaches. The other six approaches are based on the same immune optimization, but they only optimize one or two factors. MRO is our proposed approach, which optimizes message assignment order, routing, and offset. MR approach optimizes message assignment order and routing, and so on with other approaches. The algorithm was implemented in MATLAB R2018a, running on ThinkCentre M6300T computers with Intel Core i5-2400 CPUs at 3.10GHz and 8GB of RAM. Fig. 4 presents the load of the network and the percentage of schedulable messages in test cases 1-5. We are interested in the percentage of schedulable messages of the seven approaches when the message number, network scale, and load are different. The results show that MRO approach is able to find schedulable solutions for all the test cases in Table II, whereas other approaches fail to reach 100% of schedulable messages in some cases. Only MR's performance is the closest to MRO, but it still fails to find the schedulable solution when the scale of the network becomes larger. Other approaches except MR perform poorly, particularly O approach, which cannot find a schedulable solution in any case.

div.head: B. Evaluation on Schedulability
div.p: It can be seen that the improvement of MRO mainly comes from MR. MR is able to find schedulable solutions in most cases. Even in the worst case, it still can find a solution with 95% schedulable messages. This shows that the optimization of message assignment order and routing is much more important than that of message offset. The performance of R and RO is very close to each other, indicating that the optimization of offset also has little impact on the performance of R. Approaches MO, M, and O have different levels of degradation considering the percentage of schedulable messages, but in general, they perform poorly in the test cases. Most approaches except MRO reach their highest percentage of schedulable messages when the load is less than 0.2, but the performance deteriorates quickly when the load becomes heavier. It can be concluded that only by combining the approaches can we find a solution with 100% schedulable messages.

div.head: C. Evaluation on Runtime
div.p: The runtime for test cases 1-5 under different message numbers is depicted in Fig. 5. The results show that as the number of messages and the scale of the network become larger, the runtime of MRO approach generally increases. However, it is able to find a schedulable solution in a relatively short time, and the maximum runtime in the test cases is less than 600 seconds. This is because the number of iterations in MRO is always less than 500, which means that the proposed approach can find feasible solutions effectively. It can be noticed that the runtime of the different 7 approaches can be divided into 3 groups. The first group consists of MRO and MR. The runtime of these two approaches is comparatively short. When the number of chips in the network is no more than 8, the two curves basically coincide. But when MR is not able to find a schedulable solution within a certain number of iterations, as is shown in Fig. 4, its runtime increases significantly. Approaches M, R, and RO are in the second group. Their runtime is similar, and the curves of R and RO have a high degree of coincidence, which is consistent with the results in section V.B. Approaches MO and O are the last group. Their runtime increases significantly when the message number becomes larger. Among all approaches, the optimization of offset has the minimal impact on the results.

We can conclude from the analysis above that the runtime of MRO and MR are the closest among all approaches. As for approaches M, R, and RO, although they cannot find a feasible solution within 500 generations, the time of search in one generation is not too long compared with MO and O. The optimization of message offset does not make a difference in improving search efficiency.

div.head: D. Evaluation on the Number of Iterations
div.p: We choose one message set per test case in test cases 2 -5 to examine their affinity evolution curves when using MRO approach. Each message set consists of 30 pieces of messages. When the number of immune individuals and the number of cloned individuals is both 10, the affinity evolution curves are presented as follows in Fig. 6. On one hand, it can be seen that the curves of the 4 cases all have a large descending gradient and a fast convergence rate, indicating that the approach is able to find a feasible solution within a limited number of iterations. On the other hand, with the expansion of the network scale, the number of iterations does not necessarily increase. In other words, there is no direct relation between the network scale and the number of iterations. This is because the number of iterations also depends on other factors, like the number of messages in the network and the initial status before optimization. Since the number of messages in these test cases are the same, the initial status must have played a major role in deciding the number of iterations. The initialization in MRO approach is based on experience, which is not an accurate calculation, the initial status may be so poor that it takes the immune operation a long time to search for a solution that minimizes the cost function.

Since the number of iterations can greatly influence the runtime, it is essential to minimize the number of iterations in order to improve the efficiency of the algorithm. Three major factors influence the number of iterations: the number of messages in the network, the scale of the network, and the initial status before optimization. Among the three factors, only the initial status can be modified, and as is mentioned above, different initial status can make a real difference to the number of iterations. Therefore, the initialization process should be optimized, which is the direction of our future work.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: In this paper, a scheduling and routing synthesis for offchip interconnection architecture was presented using immune algorithm, which provides feasible scheduling and routing solutions for time-triggered off-chip communication. The approach focuses on the optimization of the order of message assignment, routing, and message offset. The performance evaluation results show that the approach achieves a significant improvement in schedulability and runtime.
Future work will explore mechanisms to optimize the initialization process in order to reduce the number of iterations and further improve the efficiency of the approach.
